title: Onboard contract and eval-runner shims to decouple datasets/prompts
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a lightweight, versioned onboarding contract and pluggable eval-runner shims so the benchmark/profile generator can accept arbitrary dataset and prompt sources without bespoke adapters. This work reduces coupling between model metadata, dataset sampling, and runner execution and enables predictable profile artifacts for publishing.

Goals:
- Define a stable onboarding contract schema for model metadata + pinning rules (model_id, model_version, compatible_quant, alias list, fallback chain).
- Implement adapter interfaces (dataset-adapter, prompt-adapter) that normalize incoming dataset/prompt sources to a canonical sample stream (JSONL with seed metadata).
- Introduce eval-runner shims that expose a single runner API while supporting multiple execution environments: local python runners, dockerized model runners, and remote RPC runners.
- Ensure deterministic seeding and KV-cache warmup hooks so performance profiles are comparable across environments and runs.
- Produce a canonical artifact format for performance profiles (metadata header + per-sample latencies/quality metrics) consumable by the profile publisher.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Schema is intentionally minimal: keep model pinning and compatibility rules lightweight to avoid frequent migrations. Extended attributes go in an optional `annotations` map.
- Runner shims will favor a sync API surface for simplicity; async adapters can be implemented later if needed.
- Deterministic seeding uses a two-tier seed: global harness seed + sample index to avoid correlated prompts. This adds reproducibility at the cost of some UX complexity when re-running ad-hoc.
- We will not (in this ticket) implement automatic kernel selection or hardware-specific optimizations; focus is on end-to-end portability.

Acceptance criteria:
- onboarding_contract.yaml schema landed and validated against at least 3 example models (two open-source variants + an internal quantized build).
- dataset-adapter and prompt-adapter produce identical canonical streams for two different raw dataset formats (SQuAD-like and instruction-tuning CSV).
- eval-runner shim implementations for local python and dockerized runner exist and pass the same integration tests producing comparable latency distributions within a defined tolerance.
- generated performance profile artifacts conform to the publisher schema and upload successfully to the profile registry.
- Documentation: onboarding contract doc + quickstart examples added to the benchmark docs.

Telemetry / metrics to track:
- % of onboarding runs that complete end-to-end without adapter errors.
- variance in median latency between runner types for the same model and sample set.
- time-to-first-artifact (seconds) from job start to artifact upload.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Non-determinism across runners could produce noisy profiles. Mitigation: strict seeding + warmup hooks + run-level metadata recorded.
- Schema breakage for older models. Mitigation: schema versioning and backward compatibility checks in the loader.
- Overly generic adapters increasing complexity. Mitigation: start with minimal surface and iterate based on real dataset examples.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge schema + adapters behind feature flag (bench_v2).
2) Run nightly compatibility sweep against existing profile catalog.
3) Flip flag for internal teams; collect feedback and iterate.
4) Public rollout after 2 weeks of stable results and docs updated.
